# A grid row forwards mounted and theme to its cell components, but not windowId

## Context

Measured live on 2026-09-04 by the popup-birth arm for D#18224 (`apps/workstation` at `dev@2ee23d7801`, Playwright e2e rig, scratch spec `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/PopupBirthArm.spec.mjs`, untracked). The Feed pane — `Workstation.view.FeedPane`, a `grid.Container` with a `sparkline` column — was popped out into a real popup window through the production tab action. The grid subtree moved as the same instance (20 descendants, 0 lost, consistency 4/4/4, same provider and store), every descendant in the items tree took the popup's `windowId` — and every sparkline canvas that travelled with the grid went blank.

Receipt: the five pre-existing `Neo.component.Sparkline` cells kept the **opener's** `windowId` and read `offscreenRegistered: false` for the whole 5 s settle poll; the three cells the grid created after the hop (row pool grown for the larger vessel) carry the popup's `windowId` and registered at once. Screenshots: before, the Live column draws a sparkline in every row; after, the Live column is empty in every row of the popup.

## The Problem

`Neo.grid.Row` extends `component.Base`, not a container (`src/grid/Row.mjs:39–42`). It owns its cell components in `this.components` (`:155–184`) and forwards two lifecycle configs by hand: `mounted` (`afterSetMounted`, `:84–92`, added for #9107 so canvases re-register after a VDOM purge) and `theme` (`afterSetTheme`, `:100–108`). It has no `afterSetWindowId`. `grid.Body#afterSetWindowId` (`src/grid/Body.mjs:671–681`) forwards to its rows and stops there. After a cross-window move, `grid.Container` → `grid.View` → `grid.Body` → every row carries the new id, and every pooled cell component keeps the old one. `column/Component#cellRenderer` (`src/grid/column/Component.mjs:159–171`) stamps `windowId` only at creation, which is why the three new cells were right.

For a canvas cell the consequence is total. `component/Canvas#afterSetMounted` (`src/component/Canvas.mjs:50–91`) re-transfers the canvas on remount with `transferCanvasToWorker({componentId, nodeId, windowId})`; with the stale id the request goes to the opener's main thread, where the node no longer exists, so the promise never resolves and `offscreenRegistered` stays false. `Canvas#afterSetWindowId` (`:102–108`) already resets the flag on an id change so the remount can re-register — the hook exists, the cascade never reaches it. Any component cell with window-scoped main-thread state fails the same way.

## The Architectural Reality

- `container.Base#afterSetWindowId` (`src/container/Base.mjs:319–338`) cascades to items, layout and sort zone. Rows are not containers, so they forward by hand, as they already do for `mounted` and `theme`.
- #9107 (2026-02) established the pattern for `mounted`; `theme` followed; `windowId` is the third config the row must relay.
- D#18224 row 8 / Euclid's provider-topology correction: realm registrations are re-armed by the component that owns them through `afterSetWindowId`. This defect is the one missing link in that chain for grids.

## The Fix

`Neo.grid.Row#afterSetWindowId(value, oldValue)`: call super, then for every key in `this.components` set `components[key].windowId = value` when `value` is set — the exact twin of `afterSetMounted`. Fold the three loops into one small forwarding helper so a fourth config never needs a fourth copy.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid.Row#afterSetWindowId` (new) | `container.Base:319` cascade contract; #9107 precedent | pooled cell components take the row's new `windowId` | none needed — cells without window-scoped state ignore it | Row docblock line 36 (component management) | popup arm: 8/8 canvases in the popup carry its id and `offscreenRegistered: true` |

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit, red-first: a `grid.Row` holding a component cell receives `windowId = 'w2'`; the cell reports `'w2'` (today it keeps the old value).
- [ ] Unit: a `Neo.component.Canvas` cell in a moved row resets `offscreenRegistered` and re-registers with the new `windowId` on remount (spy on `transferCanvasToWorker`, assert its `windowId` argument).
- [ ] Headed: the popup-birth arm's data-pane test passes — every canvas inside the popup pane carries the popup `windowId`, is mounted and `offscreenRegistered: true`, and the Live column is drawn in the popup.
- [ ] No behaviour change for single-window grids.

## Out of Scope

- The grid view's scroll model resetting on remount (view `scrollTop` 126 → 0 and body `startIndex` 2 → 0 in the same arm) — a separate finding, reported on D#18224.
- The owner-design work on D#18224.

## Avoided Traps

- Fixing it at the column (`column/Base#afterSetWindowId` only inserts theme files) or in the body: the row owns the pool and already forwards lifecycle configs.
- Re-creating cells on a window change: instance permanence is the point of the hop.

Registration is ownership, not drawing: the sparkline renderer's register, updateData and
updateSize run in the Canvas worker after offscreenRegistered flips and record nothing the App
Worker can be asked about, so an arm that stops at offscreenRegistered can stay green over a
blank Live column. The drawn result is now read where it lands — an element screenshot of each
travelled canvas in the popup, decoded by a small PNG helper and counted as pixels unlike the
cell's background. A canvas whose control lives in a worker reads as blank from page script
(drawImage of the placeholder copies nothing), which is why the read is a screenshot and why
the arm validates the instrument on the opener's visibly drawn cells before judging the popup.
The docblock states the execution mode truthfully: Playwright's default headless mode of the
local Chrome channel."
